message.content:
Based on my search, here is comprehensive information about **calcium-containing foods**:

## Dairy Products (Highest Natural Sources)

Dairy products are among the most concentrated and best-absorbed sources of calcium:

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Yogurt, plain low-fat (8 oz) | 415 mg |
| Milk, nonfat (1 cup) | 299 mg |
| Milk, whole (1 cup) | 276 mg |
| Mozzarella, part-skim (1.5 oz) | 333 mg |
| Cheddar cheese (1.5 oz) | 306 mg |
| Cottage cheese, 1% fat (1 cup) | 138 mg |
| Ricotta, part-skim (1/2 cup) | 337 mg |

## Non-Dairy Animal Sources

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Sardines, canned with bones (3 oz) | 325 mg |
| Salmon, pink canned with bones (3 oz) | 181 mg |

## Plant-Based Sources

### Vegetables and Leafy Greens
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Collard greens, cooked (1 cup) | 324 mg |
| Kale, cooked (1 cup) | 177-94 mg (varies by preparation) |
| Bok choy (1 cup) | 74-158 mg |
| Broccoli, cooked (1 cup) | 62-76 mg |
| Turnip greens, boiled (1/2 cup) | 99 mg |
| Okra, stir-fried (3.5 oz) | 220 mg |

**Note:** Spinach contains high levels of oxalic acid, which significantly reduces calcium absorption (only ~5% absorbed vs. ~30% from dairy). Kale, broccoli, and bok choy have better bioavailability.

### Legumes and Soy Products
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Tofu, firm made with calcium sulfate (1/2 cup) | 253-553 mg |
| Tofu, soft made with calcium sulfate (1/2 cup) | 138 mg |
| Edamame, cooked (1 cup) | 130 mg |
| Soybeans, cooked (1/2 cup) | 131 mg |

### Nuts and Seeds
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Chia seeds (1 tablespoon) | 76 mg |
| Chia seeds (1 oz) | 179 mg |
| Almonds (1 oz) | 76 mg |
| Sesame seeds/tahini (1 tbsp) | 64 mg |

### Fruits
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Dried figs (4) | 54 mg |
| Orange (1 medium) | 60-65 mg |
| Blackberries (1 cup) | 42 mg |

## Calcium-Fortified Foods

Many processed foods are fortified with calcium:

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Orange juice, calcium-fortified (1 cup) | 349 mg |
| Soy milk, fortified (1 cup) | 299-399 mg |
| Almond milk, fortified (1 cup) | 482 mg |
| Rice milk, fortified (1 cup) | 300 mg |
| Breakfast cereals, fortified (1 serving) | 100-1,000 mg |

## Other Sources

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Sesame seeds (3.5 oz) | 670 mg |
| Dried skimmed milk powder (3.5 oz) | 1,590 mg |
| White bread (3.5 oz) | 177 mg |

## Key Points About Calcium Absorption

- **Dairy products and fortified foods**: ~30% absorption rate
- **Certain plant foods** (broccoli, kale, bok choy): Similar absorption to milk when low in oxalates
- **Spinach and high-oxalate foods**: Only ~5% absorption due to oxalic acid binding calcium
- **Vitamin D** is essential for proper calcium absorption

Adults up to age 50 need about 1,000 mg of calcium daily; women over 50 and men over 70 need 1,200 mg daily.

Sources:
1. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium-HealthProfessional/
2. https://www.health.harvard.edu/nutrition/calcium-rich-foods-how-to-boost-your-intake-of-this-important-mineral
3. https://www.health.harvard.edu/diet-and-nutrition/calcium-rich-foods-how-to-boost-your-intake-of-this-important-mineral
4. https://www.webmd.com/food-recipes/guide/calcium-vitamin-d-foods
5. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK45523/table/ch7.t2/
6. https://www.webmd.com/diet/foods-high-in-calcium
7. https://gp-training.hee.nhs.uk/windsor/wp-content/uploads/sites/96/2021/09/Vitamin-D-testing-and-treatment-guidelines.pdf
8. https://imsear.searo.who.int/bitstreams/99ce16a3-83a5-4fba-8f33-d0c9a0428303/download
9. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_307FM.pdf
10. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_834FM.pdf?uid=598797444&uid2=2020111220184122
